full_judgment:
2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that the present petitioner had a contract with the opposite party in respect of embankment work at Patenga, Chittagong. While the Said work was going in full swing a devastating cyclone occurred on 20-4-91 causing serious' damage to the project and loss to the petitioner which adversely affected the continuation of the contract works. The petitioner maintained his organisation and staff and continued the work as far as possible awaiting final instruction and order from the opposite party but instead of giving proper instruction in the circumstances the opposite party terminated the contract which caused serious loss to the petitioner who demanded compensation from the opposite party, which was rejected. Then the petitioner issued a notice under clause 67 of the General Conditions of the Contract for arbitration but he was informed by the Executive Engineer that since the Bangladesh Water Development Board has decided the matter, there was no scope for hearing on the matter. Thereafter the petitioner sent a notice for appointment of arbitrator under section 9(b) of the Arbitration Act. 1940 on 15-9-93. appointing Mr. Justice Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, a formar Judge of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court, as Arbitrator and requested the opposite party either to concur in the said appointment of arbitrator or to nominate another arbitrator from their side, if they so desire. That notice was received by the opposite party, but they have not nominated any other Arbitrator as required under the law and thereafter at the request of the petitioner Mr. justice Abdur Rahman Chowdhury constituted himself as the sole Arbitrator and he sat over the matter and gave the award. None from the opposite party appeared to contest the claim of the present petitioner. Thereafter the award was produced before the aforesaid court with a prayer for making the same the Rule of the court with a prayer for notifying the opposite parties for hearing the matter and pronounce the judgment according to the award, whereupon Title Suit No. 284 of 1993 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was registered. Thereafter the opposite party filed a written objection under sections 30 and 33 of the Arbitration Act along with a surety signed by the Chairman of the Water Development Board on behalf of the Board and prayed for acceptance of the Surety, for the amount of the award which is Taka 4,95,29,000.00. Thereafter the matter was placed before the learned Subordinate Judge on 29-6-94 for hearing acceptance or otherwise of the surety. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the Advocates of both the sides and on perusal of the surety by order passed on that date accepted the surety. 

 3. The present petitioner being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with this order moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Waded Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party, on the other hand, submits that the security has been furnished in respect of the matter as per provision of section 33 of the Arbitration Act. He contends that in the Arbitration Act more particularly in section 33 of the Act it has not been provided that while furnishing security in such matters the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure shall have to be complied with or those will be applicable in such a proceeding. The learned Advocate contends that in section 33 of the Arbitration Act there is no mention how a security is to be furnished. The mode of furnishing security has not been provided for in the Act itself. He further contends that security that has been given on behalf of the Board and the Chairman of the Board was fully authorised to execute such a security and this has satisfied the provision of section 33 of the Arbitration Act as amended and that is sufficient compliance. He further submits that the wore security has not been defined either in the Arbitration Act or even. in the Code of Civil Procedure and the term security "does include the words surety and guarantee which may be provided for by any surety". Placing the relevant me of the Board Mr. Bhuiyan submits that proposal for furnishing surety by the Board was taken up by the Chairman and Members Administration and Finance and all three of them concurred on furnishing security and according to that decision the Chairman furnished security as per section 33 of Arbitration Act. 

 7. It has been provided in section 33 of the Arbitration Act, that no application challenging the existence or validity of an award or for having its effect determined shall be entertained by the court unless the applicant has deposited in the court the amount which he is required to pay under the award or has furnished security to the satisfaction of the court for the payment of such sum or for the fulfilment of any other Obligation by him under the award. 

 8. According to the opposite party they have furnished proper security as required under this provision of the Arbitration Act. This amended provision is meant for assuring the recovery of the award money if the objection is rejected against the award. Admittedly the word security has not been defined in the Code of Civil Procedure or in the Arbitration Act. Now what is the purpose of the surety. We have considered the amended provision and we are of the view that this provision has been incorporated in the Act for making sure the payment in case of success of the plaintiff. The provision under Order 25, rule 1, Order 38 rule 5 and Order 41, rule 5 prescribed certain forms for giving security and in those forms there is provision for including certain properties for the purpose of ensuring realisation of the amount mentioned in the security without any further trouble in case of success of the party in the litigation. The purpose therefore is easy realisation of the amount involved. There is therefore no dispute over that. The word security means anything which makes the money more secure or more easily recoverable.
